verses.text: Then Jesus told them a story to show that they should always pray and not give up.
He said, "In a certain town there was a judge who did not fear God and did not care about people.
A widow in that town kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against the person who is against me!'
For a while he refused. But finally he said to himself, 'Even though I do not fear God or care about people,
yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise she will wear me out by coming again and again.'"
The Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.
Will God not give justice to his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep putting them off?
I tell you, he will give them justice quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He also told this story to some who were sure they were right with God and looked down on everyone else.
"Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, 'God, I thank you that I am not like other people: robbers, evildoers, those who are unfaithful in marriage, or even like this tax collector.
I go without food twice a week, and I give a tenth of all I get.'
But the tax collector stood far off. He would not even look up to heaven. He beat his chest and said, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'
I tell you, this man, and not the other, went home right with God. Everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up."
People were also bringing babies to Jesus so that he would touch them. When the followers saw this, they told the people off.
But Jesus called the children to him and said, "Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them, because the kingdom of God belongs to people like these.
I tell you for certain, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it."
A certain ruler asked him, "Good Teacher, what must I do to receive eternal life?"
Jesus asked him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about anyone. Honour your father and your mother.'"
He said, "I have kept all these since I was young."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
When the man heard this, he became very sad, because he was very rich.
Jesus saw how sad he was and said, "How hard it is for rich people to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus replied, "What is impossible with people is possible with God."
Peter said, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Jesus said, "I tell you for certain, no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
will fail to receive many times as much in this life, and in the age to come, eternal life."
Jesus took the twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will come true.
He will be handed over to the Gentiles. They will mock him, treat him shamefully, and spit on him.
They will whip him and kill him. On the third day he will rise again."
The followers did not understand any of this. Its meaning was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what he said.
As Jesus came near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road, begging.
When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
They told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."
He called out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Those in front told him off and said he should be quiet, but he shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" "Lord, I want to see again," he replied.
Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you."
Straight away he could see, and he followed Jesus, giving glory to God. When all the people saw it, they praised God.
